spans.s:
vākyabheda
(‘split of sentences’)
------------------------------------------
This is an important principle adopted by the पूर्वमीमाṁसा works to decide the correct meaning of a Vedic text.
The same principle is resorted to, by the dharmaśāstra works also.
The doctrine of वाक्यभेद can be understood in two ways. If there are two vākyas or sentences which are equally independent, neither needing the help of the words of the other to complete it, they should be treated as two separate sentences. This is the first sense.
The second sense is as follows: Suppose that in one sentence one विधि or injunction is given and several other related factors have also been added. If these latter factors are considered further vidhis, then, the defect of वाक्यभेद arises. If on the other hand, they are treated as arthavādas—eulogies to strengthen the sense of the विधि already stated—there is no वाक्यभेद.
This principle of वाक्यभेद has often been resorted to by the commentators of Vedic works and dharmaśāstra-treatises to fix the correct meaning of the originals.
